patterns.title: One alert per item explodes into hundreds
An alert counts history instead of current state
Ansible parses a task differently than it reads
A unit runs before what it needs is ready
Session state held by a browser or client outlives what it points at
CI passes but the deployment fails
CI's environment differs from the lab's
A client retries forever against something meant to be off
Two mechanisms start the same thing
Units that can't work in a container fail there
A dashboard query returns a shape the panel doesn't expect
A default that is reasonable in general is wrong here
Not enough disk for the next change
Machines that untrusted people use share a network with the management plane
Code that only ever ran on a host prepared by hand
State made by hand that the repo neither creates nor checks
A service is turned off on purpose, and something generated or packaged still depends on it
Two automated jobs need the same lock, and one gives up
Work in flight is lost when the process holding it restarts or dies
A host missed something every host should have
A failure the monitoring can't see, or sees but tells nobody
Nested virtualization behaves differently from bare metal
An update is installed but the running processes still use the old code
Per-connection units pile up as failed
Work done inside a RAM-backed installer runs out of memory
A single-file bind mount keeps serving the old file
Two writers fight over one object
The layer under the managed stack changes on its own schedule
A safety net is configured but its result is never checked
An upstream release changed behaviour the lab relied on
An outside service the lab depends on is briefly down

plans.title: Recovery readiness, before the interview on Tue 2026-11-10
Close the monitoring's blind spots and deliver its alerts
Capacity headroom and housekeeping on pve01 and mgmt01
Bring hand-made infrastructure state and secret rotation into git
Separate visitors' workstations from the management plane
